content: At present, there are no medications approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) specifically for the treatment of nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH). Consequently, the management of NASH in individuals with type 2 diabetes primarily focuses on achieving optimal glucose control and promoting weight loss. Pioglitazone has demonstrated efficacy in improving steatohepatitis and reducing liver fibrosis. Similarly, certain GLP-1 receptor agonists have also been shown to be effective in addressing these conditions. These agents are recommended for use in patients who have significant liver fibrosis, defined as fibrosis stage F2 or greater.
